added_models.model: Syngeneic BALB/c A20 lymphoma, first-generation anti-mouse-CD19 CD3zeta (amCD19z) CAR T cells after 6 Gy TBI

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; J Immunol full text paywalled.
engagement.model: Syngeneic BALB/c A20 lymphoma, first-generation anti-mouse-CD19 CD3zeta (amCD19z) CAR T cells after 6 Gy TBI
engagement.note: Host B cells depleted 7 days after amCD19z T-cell transfer, then returned to normal as CAR T cells were lost; a transient-aplasia prediction.
engagement.short: Mouse B cells depleted, then return
engagement.quote: In the short-term (7 d after adoptive transfer), amCD19z T cells underwent Ag-dependent proliferation in vivo with a concomitant depletion in host B cell levels.
engagement.judgement: Second 2010 syngeneic system (Manchester, Gilham group): a first-generation anti-mouse-CD19 CD3zeta CAR, not the CD28-CD3zeta design of axi-cel, so product_in_model false. Cited in neither the Yescarta nor the Breyanzi SBRA (both grepped), so model_filed false. Its own track, separate from the C3H 38c13 model, because it predicted the opposite PD course (CAR T cells lost, B cells return).

engagement.magnitude_basis: B-cell depletion occurred in both; duration: mice recovered to normal levels, patients long-term aplasia in 4/8
engagement.confidence_note: Paired by me; abstract-level both sides; the model's B-cell recovery time is in the paywalled full text, so the duration gap is direction only.
engagement.model: Syngeneic BALB/c A20 lymphoma, first-generation anti-mouse-CD19 CD3zeta (amCD19z) CAR T cells after 6 Gy TBI
engagement.note: NCI trial: B-lineage depletion in patients as the readout moved in mice, but long-term in 4/8, not the transient course the model showed.
engagement.short: B cells depleted; duration unlike mice
engagement.quote: Four of the 8 patients treated on the protocol had long-term depletion of normal polyclonal CD19+ B-lineage cells.
engagement.judgement: The readout (host B-cell depletion by a CD19 CAR) moved in patients, so same in direction. The model's distinct prediction that CAR T cells would be lost and B cells return failed (CAR gene detected in all patients; long-term aplasia in 4/8) and is scored contra in safety, where it was a stated absence of autotoxicity. Alternative reading: engagement contra, because persistence was the model's headline result. Patients 1, 2 and 8 of the NCI cohort had FL (draft judgement; Table 1 unseen by the checker).
engagement.reason: B cells depleted; persistence unlike mice

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; J Immunol full text paywalled.
efficacy.model: Syngeneic BALB/c A20 lymphoma, first-generation anti-mouse-CD19 CD3zeta (amCD19z) CAR T cells after 6 Gy TBI
efficacy.note: amCD19z T cells eradicated 12-day established disseminated A20 lymphoma after 6 Gy TBI; no FL model.
efficacy.quote: These T cells also eradicated a 12-d established disseminated A20 lymphoma in mice preconditioned with 6 Gy total body irradiation.
efficacy.judgement: Same track as the engagement opener; A20 is a BALB/c B-cell lymphoma line, not FL. Nobody relied on this model for a member product.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: A20 eradication in mice vs partial remissions in FL patients
efficacy.confidence_note: Paired by me; abstract-level; three FL patients (partial remissions), direction only.
efficacy.model: Syngeneic BALB/c A20 lymphoma, first-generation anti-mouse-CD19 CD3zeta (amCD19z) CAR T cells after 6 Gy TBI
efficacy.note: NCI trial: 6/8 remissions, FL patients in partial remission; eradication of A20 in mice matched in direction; paired by me.
efficacy.short: FL remissions as A20 mice predicted
efficacy.quote: Six of the 8 patients treated on our protocol obtained remissions of their advanced, progressive B-cell malignancies.
efficacy.judgement: Mice were cured; FL patients 1 and 8 had partial remissions and patient 2 died before evaluation (draft judgement on Table 1). The NCI FMC63-CD28-CD3zeta CAR is the construct licensed as KTE-C19/axi-cel, so these patients count as treated with a member (as the draft scores them). Not neg: no member drug has failed in FL. Phase 1 response read-out scored as the primary endpoint.

patient_trials.quote: Six of the 8 patients treated on our protocol obtained remissions of their advanced, progressive B-cell malignancies.

efficacy.reason: FL remissions matched A20 mouse direction

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; J Immunol full text paywalled.
safety.model: Syngeneic BALB/c A20 lymphoma, first-generation anti-mouse-CD19 CD3zeta (amCD19z) CAR T cells after 6 Gy TBI
safety.note: Stated prediction: transient B-cell loss, CAR T cells lost, no autotoxicity over an extended period in tumour-free or tumour-bearing mice.
safety.short: Mice: no autotoxicity, B cells return
safety.quote: Importantly, no overt clinical signs of autotoxicity were observed in tumor-free or tumor-bearing mice treated with amCD19z T cells over an extended period of time.
safety.judgement: A stated prediction, not silence: the paper's point is that native CD19 on host B cells limits CAR T-cell engraftment, so B-cell loss is transient and no autotoxicity follows. The opposite of the C3H model's prolonged-depletion warning.

safety.magnitude_basis: model: B cells returned to normal levels, no autotoxicity; patients: long-term B-cell aplasia in 4/8 with hypogammaglobulinemia (IVIg)
safety.confidence_note: Paired by me; abstract-level; the hypogammaglobulinemia/IVIg sentence is body text the checker could not see, the abstract's long-term depletion sentence carries the status.
safety.model: Syngeneic BALB/c A20 lymphoma, first-generation anti-mouse-CD19 CD3zeta (amCD19z) CAR T cells after 6 Gy TBI
safety.note: Patients had long-term B-lineage depletion (4/8), later hypogammaglobulinemia needing IVIg: the opposite of the model's no-autotoxicity, B-cell-return prediction.
safety.short: Long-term B-cell aplasia, model said transient
safety.quote: Four of the 8 patients treated on the protocol had long-term depletion of normal polyclonal CD19+ B-lineage cells.
safety.judgement: The model's stated safety prediction (no autotoxicity; B-cell loss transient because CAR T cells fail to persist against native CD19) was contradicted by the first FL-containing cohort, while the filed C3H model predicted prolonged depletion and was right. Cytokine toxicity (4/8 patients) is not scored here: under decision 4 and the adjudicated species rule the mouse's silence on CRS is not a miss at 2011, and rule 7 bars using Cheadle 2014 (BALB/c acute toxicity with CD28 CARs) to rescore it. magnitude opposite: a predicted absence of harm that appeared.

added_models.model: Syngeneic BALB/c A20 lymphoma, second-generation anti-mouse-CD19 CD28-CD3zeta CAR T cells in preconditioned mice (acute cytokine-toxicity model)

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; J Immunol full text paywalled (OUP), so the CAR names and toxic cell doses are unseen.
safety.model: Syngeneic BALB/c A20 lymphoma, second-generation anti-mouse-CD19 CD28-CD3zeta CAR T cells in preconditioned mice (acute cytokine-toxicity model)
safety.note: Built after clinical cytokine toxicity was known: CD28-CD3zeta CARs gave T-cell-dose-dependent acute toxicity with raised Th1 serum cytokines in preconditioned BALB/c mice.
safety.quote: T cells armed with either CAR eliminated A20 B cell lymphoma in vivo; however, one construct induced a T cell dose-dependent acute toxicity associated with a raised serum Th1 type cytokine profile on transfer into preconditioned mice.
safety.judgement: A different system from Cheadle 2010 (second-generation CD28 CAR; acute toxicity as the read-out) and from the filed C3H model (toxicity absent in C3H and C57BL/6 recipients of the same CARs), so its own track. Sibling CAR (anti-mouse CD19 with axi-cel's CD28-CD3zeta signalling), product_in_model false; in neither SBRA, model_filed false. The opener and the retrodiction share the year because the model's first use is the retrodiction.

safety.magnitude_basis: acute toxicity after CAR T-cell transfer with raised Th1 cytokines (IFN-gamma, TNF)
safety.confidence_note: Paired: the paper's Introduction and Discussion, which would carry any stated comparison with the clinical cytokine toxicities, are paywalled, so comparison_stated is false; abstract-level on both sides.
safety.model: Syngeneic BALB/c A20 lymphoma, second-generation anti-mouse-CD19 CD28-CD3zeta CAR T cells in preconditioned mice (acute cytokine-toxicity model)
safety.note: Retrodiction: mouse acute toxicity with raised Th1 cytokines reproduces the IFN-gamma/TNF-correlated acute toxicities of the 2011 NCI cohort (3 FL); paired by me.
safety.quote: Four of the 8 treated patients had prominent elevations in serum levels of the inflammatory cytokines IFNγ and TNF.
safety.judgement: Year 2014: the comparison could not exist before the model paper (epub 2014-03-12); epub and print years are those of the patient-side src. Cytokine toxicity was known from the 2011-2013 CD19 CAR-T reports before this model was built, so retro, never same (decision 10). It shows the filed C3H model's 2011 silence was strain-conditional, but rule 7 keeps that entry as adjudicated. No prospective test of this model's own predictions (dose-dependence; Th2-driven granulomatous chronic toxicity, never reported in patients) was found.

added_models.model: NSG mice engrafted with patient-derived ALL blasts, high-dose CART19 (CRS/neuroinflammation model; GM-CSF neutralisation with lenzilumab)

safety.confidence_note: Full text read via PMC6376281; the CAR is named only as CART19 (research-grade, Mayo), not a member product.
safety.model: NSG mice engrafted with patient-derived ALL blasts, high-dose CART19 (CRS/neuroinflammation model; GM-CSF neutralisation with lenzilumab)
safety.note: Built after the fact: NSG mice with patient ALL blasts and 2-5 x 10^6 CART19 cells develop CRS and neuroinflammation; lenzilumab prevents both.
safety.short: PDX mouse: GM-CSF block prevents CRS
safety.quote: Together, these studies illuminate a novel approach to abrogate NI and CRS through GM-CSF neutralization, which may potentially enhance CAR-T cell function.
safety.judgement: Distinct from the Norelli HuSGM3 and Giavridis SCID-beige tracks: different host (NSG, not humanized), tumour (patient ALL blasts, not a line), mediator (GM-CSF) and intervention (lenzilumab), so its own track. product_in_model false; in neither SBRA, model_filed false. Opener and retrodiction share the year because the model's first use is the retrodiction.

safety.magnitude_basis: CRS (weight loss, serum cytokines) and neuroinflammation (CNS myeloid and T-cell infiltration) phenotypes
safety.confidence_note: The patient comparison is stated in the Results ('similar to what is seen in human CRS after CAR-T cell therapy') and Discussion ('Mice developed symptoms of CRS and NI'); the clinical CRS/neurotoxicity it reproduces is the ALL/NHL literature, never FL.
safety.model: NSG mice engrafted with patient-derived ALL blasts, high-dose CART19 (CRS/neuroinflammation model; GM-CSF neutralisation with lenzilumab)
safety.note: Retrodiction: the PDX mice developed CRS and neuroinflammation like patients; GM-CSF neutralisation prevented CRS and cut CNS myeloid/T-cell infiltration.
safety.short: Reproduces CRS and neuroinflammation; GM-CSF driven
safety.quote: In a patient acute lymphoblastic leukemia xenograft model of CRS and neuroinflammation (NI), GM-CSF neutralization resulted in a reduction of myeloid and T cell infiltration in the central nervous system and a significant reduction in NI and prevention of CRS.
safety.judgement: CRS and neurotoxicity were known from the 2011-2017 CD19 CAR-T trials before this model existed, so retro (decision 10). Its prospective prediction (lenzilumab prevents CRS and reduces neuroinflammation without impairing efficacy) was tested with a member drug in ZUMA-19, the next entry.

safety.magnitude_basis: all-grade CRS and neurologic event rates with lenzilumab vs ZUMA-1 axi-cel alone (CRS 93%, neurologic events 64%)
safety.confidence_note: n=6, single-arm 3+3 phase 1; the phase 2 primary (grade >=2 neurologic events within 28 days) was never measured; registry outcome values only, no peer-reviewed report found.
safety.model: NSG mice engrafted with patient-derived ALL blasts, high-dose CART19 (CRS/neuroinflammation model; GM-CSF neutralisation with lenzilumab)
safety.note: ZUMA-19 (lenzilumab + axi-cel, LBCL, n=6): neurologic events 100% and 67%, CRS 67% per cohort, serious encephalopathy 3/6; phase 2 never run.
safety.quote: Phase 1 and Phase 2: Percentage of Participants Experiencing Neurologic Events
safety.judgement: First prospective test of the model's prediction with a member drug (decision 10), scored as usual. The model predicted prevention of CRS and a significant reduction in neuroinflammation; with lenzilumab 4/6 patients had CRS and 5/6 neurologic events (serious encephalopathy 3/6, serious aphasia 1/6), against ZUMA-1's 93% CRS and 64% neurologic events for axi-cel alone, so not prevented and no evident reduction: contra in direction at low confidence. Humanigen's press release of 2021-04-20 (tier 5, the earliest public report) framed the same six patients as positive (no severe CRS or neurotoxicity at 1800 mg; one 2-day grade-3 neurotoxicity at 600 mg; ORR 83%); the registry is the higher-tier record of the same trial and sets the status, and dating by the press release would move this entry to 2021 with the status unchanged. Alternative reading: same with source_calls_it partial, on grade >=3 CRS 0/6 and grade >=3 neurotoxicity 1/6 against ZUMA-1's 13% and 28%, which n=6 cannot distinguish from no effect. Program terminated 2022, 'not due to any safety concerns' (registry). LBCL patients, hence imported_from DLBCL; product_in_model refers to the model's research CART19.

considered_not_added: Giavridis SCID-beige Raji CRS track's prospective test (Park 2023 CRS 74% all-grade; Blood Adv 2025 once-daily anakinra insufficient): existing track scid-beige-raji-crs-mouse, so not an added model; needs a dated entry on that track in the draft

Liso-cel Raji/NSG track safety opener (Breyanzi SBRA: 'BREYANZI does not survive in immunocompetent rodents and induces graft-versus-host disease in immunocompromised mice'): existing track raji-nsg-xenograft-fmc63-41bb-car, belongs in the draft, not here
Taraseviciute 2018 rhesus macaque CD20 CAR-T neurotoxicity model: anti-CD20 CAR, another drug class, set aside under decision 13
Brentjens 2003 SCID-beige Raji with 19z1/19-28z (MSKCC): not a member's model; the SCID-beige Raji system already carries the Giavridis track
Nalm-6 and other CD19+ line xenografts in NSG mice: the same immunodeficient-xenograft system class as the tracked Raji/NSG track; Breyanzi SBRA redacts the lines; no FL comparison
FL patient-derived tumoroid (ASH 2024 abstract, ARI-0001 CAR-T): not a member product, conference abstract, no patient comparison

Axi-cel population QSP model of CAR-T phenotypes (Cancers 2021, PMC8199881) and the liso-cel population cellular-kinetics model (Certara/BMS): retrospective patient exposure-response at the standard dose, not a model used to choose a dose; liso-cel's dose came from TRANSCEND dose-finding
Patient-level clinical predictors of axi-cel outcome in FL (JCI 2024: TNF-alpha, IL-12p40; ZUMA-5 product attributes): clinical biomarkers, not a model system
Relma-cel (JWCAR029) nonclinical package: NMPA review not public; shares the liso-cel construct; no separate model found
Tisagenlecleucel (ELARA) and tafasitamab (inMIND) FL data and their models: not members; not widened
Humanigen 2021-04-20 ZUMA-19 press release (tier 5): same six patients as the 2024 registry record, which outranks it and sets the status; recorded in the judgement, not as its own entry
